5  Overview of SPSS data

5.1 Package set up and load data


library(here)
## here() starts at /Users/joecrowley/R/Exploratory
library(haven)
library(tidyverse)
## ── Attaching core tidyverse packages ──────────────────────── tidyverse 2.0.0 ──
## ✔ dplyr     1.1.4     ✔ readr     2.1.5
## ✔ forcats   1.0.0     ✔ stringr   1.5.1
## ✔ ggplot2   4.0.0     ✔ tibble    3.2.1
## ✔ lubridate 1.9.4     ✔ tidyr     1.3.1
## ✔ purrr     1.0.4
## ── Conflicts ────────────────────────────────────────── tidyverse_conflicts() ──
## ✖ dplyr::filter() masks stats::filter()
## ✖ dplyr::lag()    masks stats::lag()
## ℹ Use the conflicted package (<http://conflicted.r-lib.org/>) to force all conflicts to become errors
library(labelled)
library(flextable)
## 
## Attaching package: 'flextable'
## 
## The following object is masked from 'package:purrr':
## 
##     compose

# Load BSA teaching data
df <- readRDS(here::here("data", "synthetic_bsa2019.rds"))
source(here::here("Scripts", "freq_spss.R"))

# Add missing value label for NatFrEst = 0
labelled::val_labels(df$NatFrEst) <- c(labelled::val_labels(df$NatFrEst), c("Zero people broken law" = 0))

vars <- names(df)
labels <- df %>% var_label(unlist = T, null_action = "fill")


5.2 Contents

for (xxx in 1:length(vars)){
  # print(xxx)
  cat(paste0(" * [",vars[xxx],"]"))
  cat(" :- ")
  cat(labels[xxx])
  cat("\n")

}
  • Sserial :- Archive Serial
  • WtFactor :- Final BSA weight
  • RSex :- Sex of respondent
  • RAgeCat :- Age of respondent(grouped)<7 category> dv
  • eq_inc_quintiles :- Quintiles of total equivalised household income, net of tax, NI, disability benefits and housing costs (missings removed)
  • RClassGp :- NS-SEC analytic classes [respondent] 6 category dv
  • HEdQual3 :- Highest educational qual obtained - dv
  • Married :- Marital status <4 categories> dv
  • ChildHh :- Whether respondent has any children in household: dv
  • skipmeal :- How often do you or other members of your household skip a meal because there is not enough money for food?: SC B, C
  • paptype :- Newspaper readership (grouped)
  • SMNews :- How often, if at all, do you read the news via a social media site, such as Facebook or Twitter?
  • PartyId2 :- Party political id (compressed) dv
  • Politics :- How much interest do you have in politics?
  • SocTrust :- Generally speaking, would you say that most people can be trusted, or that you can`t be too careful in dealing with people?
  • Spend1 :- Which would be your highest priority for extra govt spending?
  • Dole :- Opinions differ about the level of benefits for unemployed people - Which comes closest to your own view
  • TaxSpend :- If it had to choose, should govt reduce/increase/maintain levels of taxation and spending?
  • MuchPov :- Some people say there is very little real poverty in Britain today - Others say there is quite a lot - Which comes closest to your view
  • Poverty1 :- Is someone in Britain in poverty if they had enough to buy the things they really needed, but not enough to buy the things most people take for
  • Poverty2 :- Is someone in Britain in poverty if they had enough to eat and live, but not enough to buy other things they needed
  • NatFrEst :- Out of every 100 people receiving benefits in Britain, how many have broken the law by giving false information to support their claim?
  • incdiffs :- Differences in income in GB are too large?: SC B, C
  • welfare2 :- Welfarism scale (welfhelp to proudwlf) dv
  • leftrigh :- Left-right scale (redistrb to indust4) dv
  • libauth :- Libertarian-authoritarian scale (TradVals to censor) dv


5.3 Variable overview

Each variable is presented below. Variables with 50 or fewer unique values are shown as a frequency table. Variables with more than 50 unique values are tested for numeric conversion: if fewer than 5% of values fail to convert, they are shown as a histogram with any non-numeric values tabulated separately; otherwise they are shown as a frequency table. Where a variable has more than 10 unique values and all convert cleanly to numeric, a histogram is shown alongside the frequency table.

for (var in vars) {

  # Get the variable label before any conversion, falling back to the variable name
  var_lbl         <- labelled::var_label(df[[var]]) %||% var

  # Convert to factor. nolabel_to_na = FALSE keeps values without labels as their
  # numeric codes rather than NAs, so numeric variables with a few labelled values
  # (e.g. a sentinel 0 = "Zero people broken law") don't lose most of their data.
  variable        <- df[[var]] %>% labelled::to_factor(user_na_to_na = TRUE, nolabel_to_na = FALSE)

  # Count unique non-missing values after factor conversion
  n_unique        <- variable %>% na.omit() %>% unique() %>% length()

  # Try converting factor levels to numeric. Labelled values produce strings like
  # "[0] Zero people broken law" which fail as.numeric() and become NA.
  # Unlabelled values produce plain numeric strings like "23" which convert fine.
  # pct_new_na is the share of originally non-missing values that fail conversion.
  numeric_attempt <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(variable)))
  original_non_na <- !is.na(variable)
  new_na          <- is.na(numeric_attempt) & original_non_na
  pct_new_na      <- sum(new_na) / sum(original_non_na) * 100

  cat("\n")
  cat("[Contents] ")
  cat("\n\n\n")
  cat("### ", var, "\n")

  # Branch 1: ≤50 unique values (likely categorical) OR ≥5% fail numeric conversion.
  # Always show a freq_spss table. Also show a histogram if the variable has more
  # than 10 unique values and fewer than 5% fail numeric conversion —
  # i.e. it is essentially numeric but has some labelled values worth tabulating.
  if (n_unique <= 50 || pct_new_na >= 5) {

    if (n_unique > 10 && pct_new_na < 5) {
      p <- ggplot(data.frame(x = numeric_attempt), aes(x = x)) +
        geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
        labs(x = var, title = var_lbl) +
        theme_minimal()
      print(p)
    }

    freq_spss(data = df, var = !!rlang::sym(var), as_flextable = TRUE) %>%
      flextable_to_rmd()

  # Branch 2: >50 unique values AND <5% fail conversion — treat as continuous.
  # Show a histogram. If any values failed numeric conversion (non-numeric labels),
  # tabulate those separately below the histogram.
  } else {

    p <- ggplot(data.frame(x = numeric_attempt), aes(x = x)) +
      geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
      labs(x = var, title = var_lbl) +
      theme_minimal()
    print(p)

    freq_spss(data = df, var = !!rlang::sym(var), as_flextable = TRUE) %>%
      flextable_to_rmd()

  }

  cat("\n")
  cat("<br>")
  cat("\n")

}
